title: Rahul Dravid-backed Disseqt AI raises $8 million led by Gresham House
summary: Rahul Dravid-backed Disseqt AI raises 8 million dollars led by Gresham House
detailed: Disseqt AI, a Dublin-headquartered startup that tests and monitors AI agents for large companies, has raised $8 million in a funding round led by Gresham House Ventures.

According to Disseqt AI, its platform conducts adversarial testing and red-teaming using at least 84 jailbreak techniques, while generating audit evidence aligned with the EU AI Act, NIST AI Risk Management Framework and ISO/IEC 42001.
The latest round follows Disseqt AI's earlier pre-seed investment in 2025, when it secured backing from Sure Valley Ventures and Delta Partners.
In April 2026, Disseqt AI investor Mindflair announced that the startup had been selected as one of eight Irish technology companies for an Enterprise Ireland accelerator programme led by 500 Global.
sentences: Disseqt AI, a Dublin-headquartered startup that tests and monitors AI agents for large companies, has raised $8 million in a funding round led by Gresham House Ventures.
Former Indian cricket captain Rahul Dravid invested in the round in his individual capacity.
Sure Valley Ventures (SVV), Delta Partners and Enterprise Ireland also took part, along with angel investors who include senior leaders from OpenAI, Palo Alto Networks, Salesforce and Meta.
Disseqt said it will use the capital to add enterprise customers around the world.
It is also hiring in India for sales, operations and technology roles, and is building a bigger team in London.

“ This funding will help us scale up our R&D in India and build our sales and marketing team in London as we scale with financial institutions, ” Apoorva Kumar, CEO and co-founder of Disseqt AI, told CiOL.
AI agents are software systems that do more than answer questions.
They handle requests, access company data and take actions inside business systems.
Disseqt sells what it calls an AI assurance platform, which checks that these agents behave as intended and stay within company policy and the law.
Companies using the platform can test applications and agents before launch, for example by checking whether an agent can be prompted to reveal confidential customer data.
Once the agent is live, the platform enforces company policies, monitors behaviour continuously, blocks outputs that breach those policies and keeps records for audits.

According to Disseqt AI, its platform conducts adversarial testing and red-teaming using at least 84 jailbreak techniques, while generating audit evidence aligned with the EU AI Act, NIST AI Risk Management Framework and ISO/IEC 42001.
The startup also cites a customer testimonial reporting that adversarial testing time was reduced from four weeks to approximately three days.
“ Every enterprise is handing real work to AI agents, but very few can prove those agents are safe, fair and within policy.
This gap often stops ambitious AI projects from going live, and it is what we built Disseqt to close, ” Kumar said.
“ We test AI agentic workflows before launch, control in real time and keep the audit trail, independently of the model providers, ” he added.
Disseqt has disclosed two deployments without naming the clients.
For a global sports league's fan engagement agent, used by 80 million fans, it said it raised the safe-response rate from 80% to 99% across tests covering safety, bias and privacy.
The startup said no unsafe outputs were found when the original failing tests were run again after fixes.
It also provides assurance for the credit card services programme of a large European bank.
Disseqt AI reaches enterprise customers through partnerships with global IT services firms and systems integrators.
Its distribution network includes HCLTech, Infosys and Mphasis, while the startup has separately announced collaborations involving Harbinger Group and Tata Technologies.
Cognizant has also been named as a partner in media reports.
Founded in late 2025 by Kumar, Manish Atri and Cyril Treacy, Disseqt brings together founders with experience at major technology companies.
Kumar previously worked at Microsoft, AWS and SAP, while Atri held roles at Cradlepoint and ColorTokens.
Treacy previously worked at Salesforce, where he was the company's 13th employee in the EMEA region, according to Disseqt.
The startup is headquartered at NovaUCD, University College Dublin's innovation centre, and has an office in London.
Its engineering and AI development is based in Koramangala, Bengaluru, and Atri works out of India.
Kumar and Atri are both graduates of IIIT Allahabad, according to media reports.
The latest round follows Disseqt AI's earlier pre-seed investment in 2025, when it secured backing from Sure Valley Ventures and Delta Partners.
Both investors participated in the new Gresham House Ventures-led round, alongside Enterprise Ireland.
In April 2026, Disseqt AI investor Mindflair announced that the startup had been selected as one of eight Irish technology companies for an Enterprise Ireland accelerator programme led by 500 Global.
Gresham House Ventures is the growth capital arm of Gresham House, a specialist alternative investment manager with £12.7 billion in assets under management.

Its deal team on Disseqt was Rohit Mathur, Hamza Rafiq and Jack Woodnott, and the firm's recent bets include payments platform Ryft, savings and mortgage platform Tembo, workplace trust platform Veremark and healthcare platform 01Health.
“ Companies need to test and control their AI with tools that sit apart from the model providers they rely on.
Disseqt does that across the full life of an AI application, and its early customers include some of the most demanding regulated buyers in Europe, ” Mathur said.
For Dravid, Disseqt is a departure from his earlier startup bets, which have been consumer brands.
According to data from Tracxn, he invested in Bombay Shaving Company's $10.6 million Series D round in November 2025 and in Good Farmer Food's $1.5 million seed round in January 2026.
